bullets.title: S&P +0.7-0.9% Monday; Mag-7 rebounds after last week's sharp underperformance
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures up ~0.9% and Nasdaq futures +1.2% Monday morning, with the index trading around 7,408. This follows a brutal prior week where Momentum/Growth indices fell 4.3%/4.1% WoW and Friday was the 4th worst day for Momentum since 2004; Mag-7 dropped ~6% EW while the other 493 S&P stocks rose 0.7%.

bullets.title: Memory shortage is the dominant macro theme across Tech: Apple hikes prices 15-25%, MU signals supply deficit through 2028
bullets.body: Apple raised Mac/iPad prices 15-25% citing unprecedented memory cost spikes; CEO Cook said he's never seen component price increases this significant or rapid, with iPhone hikes expected at the iPhone 18 launch in September. MU post-earnings commentary and Micron's $100B+ long-term memory contracts (2026-2030) signal a structural supply deficit; Elon Musk and Tim Cook both called it a 'once-in-a-century' shortage, with HBM pricing negotiations in fall 2027 expected to show triple-digit Y/Y ASP increases. Apple is reportedly lobbying the US government to source lower-cost DRAM from China's CXMT due to supply constraints.

bullets.title: Samsung/SK Hynix announce ~$3.55T combined capex through 2040; DRAM/NAND upcycle extended to at least 2Q28
bullets.body: Samsung announced Won2,450tn and SK Hynix Won1,100tn in semiconductor investments through 2040, with implied yearly cadence materially above prior UBS estimates (Samsung Won140tn/yr vs est Won75-112tn; SK Hynix Won73tn/yr vs est Won44-67tn). A new Jeonnam-Gwangju cluster will house four fabs (two per company), and SK Hynix's Yongin ramp timing was pulled forward by 12 years. UBS maintains Overweight on WFE stocks with Buy ratings on ASML, Applied Materials, Lam Research, and Tokyo Electron; the memory upcycle is seen extending at least to 2Q28E/4Q27E.

bullets.title: AI capex rotation: infrastructure beneficiaries favored over hyperscalers; mid-cycle rotation, not bull-market end
bullets.body: 22V and Citi both frame the Mag-7 sell-off as a mid-cycle rotation toward AI infrastructure beneficiaries rather than the end of the AI bull market; memory demand and token usage remain supportive. Hyperscaler buybacks are slowing (especially Google) as AI capex ramps, risking a shift from supply support to demand headwind; NVDA and MU alone account for ~40% of S&P 500 Q2 EPS growth. Elevated volatility and rich call skew on hyperscalers create attractive 6-month 1x2 costless overlay opportunities on MSFT, AMZN, ORCL, META, and NFLX.

bullets.title: Core PCE inflation sticky; pushed to 1H27; JPM forecasts US core PCE at 3.3-3.4% through mid-2026
bullets.body: Multiple strategists flag core inflation is proving stickier than forecast, with the core PCE deflator target pushed from 2H26 to 1H27. JPM's monthly inflation forecast shows US core PCE at 3.3-3.4% through July 2026, while Piper Sandler notes nominal rates remain below nominal growth and real rates below potential GDP—both supportive of persistent inflation. The Fed policy path (benign slowdown vs. persistent inflation/September hike risk) is the key macro swing factor for cyclicals vs. defensives.

bullets.title: June ISM Manufacturing tracking 54.3; Dallas Fed signals broad expansion in demand, employment, output
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised its June ISM Manufacturing PMI tracking estimate to 54.3 from 54.0 in May, with the Dallas Fed ISM-equivalent rising to 52.9 from 50.5 driven by higher employment and inventories. Employment and hours worked improved strongly; input price pressures decelerated slightly while output prices accelerated—consistent with sticky inflation in goods.

bullets.title: JPM bullish on US equities: consumer cash pile hits record $22.9T; tactically long Tech, Cyclicals
bullets.body: JPM notes the consumer cash pile (checking + savings + MMF) reached a record $22.9T in 2026Q1 vs. $14.8T in 2019Q4, with household net worth at a record $174T (+$12.8T in FY25). Credit card delinquencies are at 2.9%, the lowest since 2023Q3. JPM is tactically bullish on Tech (AI, Memory, Semis), Cyclicals (Airlines, Banks, Homebuilders, Transports), and Healthcare; real GDP forecast is 1.8% Q4/Q4 for 2026 with earnings season unofficially starting July 14.

bullets.title: Pension rebalancing and negative gamma create elevated downside risk; S&P resistance at 7,500
bullets.body: Pension rebalancing is expected to shift ~$52B out of equities into fixed income (~-1.7σ move). S&P 500 gamma is near the third-lowest on record, raising risk of volatile self-reinforcing price action, with SPX resistance at 7,500 (95th percentile gamma zone). Excess liquidity turned negative for the first time since 2021 as financial conditions tighten with terminal rate expectations rising faster than the neutral rate.

bullets.title: $160B 2026 IPO issuance not a market-top signal; net equity supply remains negative due to buybacks
bullets.body: UBS argues 2026's ~$160B US IPO issuance falls in the second quintile when adjusted for market size and that large tech deals (not broad exuberance) are driving proceeds. Net equity supply remains negative due to substantial buybacks offsetting issuance; however, rising capex may reduce buybacks and FCF, potentially making net equity supply less negative going forward.

bullets.title: Major bank capital return cycle underway: JPM $50B buyback, Morgan Stanley $20B, multiple dividend hikes
bullets.body: Following stress test results, JPMorgan Chase authorized a new $50B common share repurchase program and Morgan Stanley reauthorized a $20B multi-year equity buyback. Dividend increases were broad-based: Bank of New York Mellon +18.9%, Morgan Stanley +15.0%, Wells Fargo +11.1%, and PNC Financial +17.6%. Accenture also increased its FY26 share repurchase program by $2B.

bullets.title: Comcast to spin off NBCUniversal + Sky in ~12 months; CMCSA +22%, CHTR +24% on merger optionality
bullets.body: Comcast announced a tax-free spinoff of NBCUniversal and Sky into a separate public company (~1 year timeline), with Mike Cavanagh leading NBCU and Michael Angelakis leading the cable RemainCo. KeyBanc SOTP values the post-spin entities at high $20s/low $30s per share; multiple analysts note the separation raises the probability of a Comcast Cable/Charter merger. CMCSA is suspending share buybacks ahead of the spin; both post-spin entities expected to maintain investment-grade balance sheets.

bullets.title: Charter +24% on SpaceX mobile partnership talks; potential Starlink traffic through Spectrum network
bullets.body: Charter held executive-level talks with SpaceX on a consumer mobile phone offering that would route Starlink phone traffic through Spectrum's WiFi/small cell infrastructure. Citi cut CHTR's PT to $190 from $230 on tougher 2Q comps but maintains Buy. The SpaceX-Charter potential deal is seen putting mobile network operators in a more difficult competitive position post-CMCSA spin.

bullets.title: VZ -1%: $700-800M Q2 loss from BT JV reclassification; up to $1.55B in total Q2 charges
bullets.body: Verizon is establishing a 50:50 JV with BT Group combining international operations across 3,000+ customers and 180+ countries ($4B combined annual revenue), with a $625M equalization payment to BT. The held-for-sale reclassification triggers a $700-800M Q2 loss; combined with $350-450M severance and $200-300M asset rationalization charges, total Q2 charges reach up to ~$1.55B.

bullets.title: Enterprise AI cost constraint is accelerating open-source adoption; older models sufficient for 90%+ of agentic use cases
bullets.body: Roth's Databricks conference takeaway: enterprise apps don't need frontier LLMs—older models handle 90%+ of agentic use cases. AI costs are the key adoption constraint, driving interest in open-source models at <$0.10/mn tokens vs. Anthropic's ~$2/mn tokens. This has implications for hyperscaler inference revenue and the competitive moat of proprietary frontier models.

bullets.title: Ad ecosystem tone constructive post-Cannes; Search, Social, CTV demand healthy; LLM Search incremental
bullets.body: Post-Cannes, Citi and Roth both characterize the ad ecosystem as constructive, with Search, Social, and CTV demand healthy. CTV is shifting to programmatic and extending into live sports; Google antitrust behavioral remedy seen as a cleaner win for independent ad-tech. LLM Search demand is expected to come from incremental budgets rather than cannibalizing existing spend. AMZN advertising on ChatGPT signals AI as a meaningful customer discovery channel, with potential headwind to Amazon's search-based ad business if discovery shifts structurally to AI.

bullets.title: EM: China turns net overweight for first time since March 2025; Korea memory stocks hitting mandate limits
bullets.body: JPM EM fund survey shows consensus turned net overweight on China+HK for the first time since March 2025, though median EM fund allocation is only 10bps above benchmark. China positioning focuses on AI, energy security, and robotics. In contrast, $87B of foreign net outflows from Korea YTD would break the annual Asia record; over 90% of those outflows came from memory stocks alone, with 10% of EM investors hitting ownership mandate limits.

bullets.title: ON/SYNA $7B all-stock deal widely disliked; QCOM nearing $4B Modular AI chip acquisition
bullets.body: onsemi agreed to acquire Synaptics in an all-stock deal valued at ~$7B EV; the deal was received poorly by buyside investors, with the combined entity seen in 'deal purgatory' for 18+ months. Separately, Qualcomm is nearing a ~$4B deal to acquire AI chip company Modular Inc., with QCOM raising its data center revenue target to $15B by F29E and auto revenues to $10B—non-handset revenues targeting $40B (40% CAGR F25-29E).

bullets.title: Data center power: distributed/onsite generation scaling; 800VDC architecture driving new equipment demand
bullets.body: Data centers are migrating to 800VDC architectures, creating revenue opportunities in solid-state transformers, BESS, and rack-scale solutions. Morgan Stanley initiates Innio (INIO) at Overweight with a $47 PT, forecasting 24% revenue CAGR and 36% EBITDA CAGR through 2030 on reciprocating engine demand for on-site power. Citi forecasts 14.5 GW HPC power absorption in 2026, rising to 20 GW average for 2027-2030; VRT, ENPH, and AMSC are positioned to benefit from DC power architecture evolution.

bullets.title: June nonfarm payrolls estimated ~113k (UBS); AI displacing temp help and back-office jobs
bullets.body: UBS estimates June nonfarm payrolls at ~113k, down from 172k in May but above the 12-month average of ~57k, with unemployment expected to remain at 4.3%. Temporary help is down ~20% since March 2022 despite 6% overall payroll growth, reflecting AI displacement; accounting/tax/bookkeeping/payroll jobs fell ~8% MoM. The formal labor market report is due Thursday with a JPM economist call July 2.

bullets.title: Prediction markets and stablecoin regulation accelerating; DraftKings $11.3B annualized DKeX volume in week 1
bullets.body: DraftKings launched its proprietary prediction markets exchange (DKeX) with ~$3.4B annualized consumer volume in the week ended June 21. Meta is building a points-based prediction markets app; Charles Schwab and Cboe are planning S&P 500 binary options contracts. The OCC issued proposed rules requiring stablecoin issuers to comply with BSA/AML-CFT standards; the European Parliament is backing a digital euro with a 12-month pilot starting H2 2027.
